2026-11-17.title: Third Tuesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Faithful in little, faithful in much
2026-11-17.verse: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
theo: Paul calls the apostles “servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries,” and says: “it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.” Everything we have, money, time, faith, is entrusted to us; we are managers, not owners.

Jesus' parable of the dishonest manager is surprising: the master praises his shrewdness, not his dishonesty. If worldly people are clever with money for their own future, Christians should be wise in using wealth for eternity, “make friends for yourselves by means of dishonest wealth”, through generosity to the poor. And the conclusion is clear: “You cannot serve God and wealth.”
outline: Ask: if God audited your accounts today, what would he find?
All is entrusted; trustworthiness is required.
Use money to make friends in heaven: give to the poor.
You cannot serve God and wealth.
live: Correct one small dishonesty: a bill, a claim, a borrowed item.
Set aside a fixed part of income for the poor.
2026-11-17.prayer: Lord, all I have is yours. Make me a trustworthy steward, faithful in little things, generous with the poor, and free to serve you alone. Amen.

quick: Use wealth wisely for eternity: give.
No one can serve God and wealth.
2026-11-17.question: Who is really my master: God or money?

homily: Dear friends, Paul calls the apostles servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries, and says that it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy (1 Corinthians 4:1–2). Everything we have, money, time and faith, is entrusted to us; we are managers, not owners.

In the parable of the dishonest manager Jesus says: whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:10–13). Money is a good servant but a bad master.

Today the Church also remembers St Elizabeth of Hungary, a princess who saw her wealth as belonging to the poor. Let us set aside a share of our income for God and the poor, and honour the Lord with what we have. Amen.
kids: Children, everything we have is a gift from God. Today set aside a little of your pocket money for the poor!

intro: Paul's stewards of the mysteries and Jesus' shrewd manager teach the right use of what is entrusted to us.

points.h: Honour the Lord with your wealth
sub: All we have comes from God.
Giving the first fruits shows whom we trust.
q: Honor the LORD with your substance and with the first fruits of all your produce.
And I tell you, make friends for yourselves by means of dishonest wealth so that when it is gone, they may welcome you into the eternal homes.
points.apply: Set aside a fixed part of your income for the poor.

q: You shall have only a full and honest weight; you shall have only a full and honest measure.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.

sub: Money is a good servant and a bad master.
We are free when God alone is Lord.
q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
No slave can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
points.apply: Fast from one unnecessary purchase this week.

concl: We are stewards of God's gifts and mysteries.
2026-11-17.resolve: Review your spending this week in the light of the Gospel.
